architecture: Glm4MoeLiteForCausalLM (DeepSeek-V3-style MLA): 47 decoder layers (layer 0 dense MLP 10240, layers 1-46 MoE: 64 routed experts x 1536, top-4, 1 shared expert, routed_scaling 1.8), 20 heads, q_lora 768, kv_lora 512, qk 192+64, v 256, vocab 154880; checkpoint also holds 1 MTP layer (index 47) that HF ignores
params_note: total parameters as instantiated by transformers (meta device); the checkpoint on disk has 31.22 B (31221485568) because it also stores an unused MTP layer
active_params_note: computed from the meta model: all non-routed-expert parameters (incl. embedding + lm_head) + top-k/n_experts of the routed experts; the vendor quotes A3B (~3B active)
fits_single_80gb_detail: Yes in bf16: 59.9 GB of weights (55.8 GiB; 62.4 GB on disk incl. the ignored MTP layer) leaves ~20-24 GB on an 80 GB GPU. bitsandbytes does not help (fused expert tensors, 93% of the params, are not quantised). KV: transformers 5.0-5.14 cache the expanded per-head K/V = 962,560 B/token (~20 GB buys only ~21k tokens -> ~10 thinking sequences per batch); transformers>=5.15 cache the compressed MLA latents = 54,144 B/token (batches of 64 fit easily). Prompts of ~20k tokens or more do not fit in generate() on 5.0-5.14 (see known_issues); the registry's MAX_PROMPT_CHARS cap currently keeps them out (served prompts <= ~2.8k tokens).
weights_gb_4bit_note: not applicable: fused expert tensors are not quantised by bitsandbytes

access_check.method: HfApi.model_info + HTTP HEAD (redirects not followed) with the local HF token on config.json and the first safetensors shard (2xx/3xx = accessible, 401/403 = gated and access not granted); no weights downloaded

min_transformers_note: glm4_moe_lite first appears in v5.0.0rc3 (GitHub tag check); first stable release 5.0.0 (transformers 5.0-5.20 need Python>=3.10, 5.21+ need Python>=3.11 per PyPI metadata); NOT available in 4.57.6 (the local env): verified on 5.0.0 and 5.24.0 only
thinking_note: forced OFF: chat template enable_thinking=False puts '</think>' into the generation prompt
max_new_note: defaults of the adapter (Ctx.run(max_new=...) overrides): cot 640, reasoning/thinking 2048 (hard GPQA-style questions can exceed it -> unparsed counts wrong, watch parse_rate), direct 8
layer_path_note: attribute path starting at the loaded model object (`model`), i.e. the adapter attribute layer_path is 'model.layers'
layer_path_verified: meta device on transformers 5.0.0 (the class does not exist on 4.57.6): `model.model.layers` is a ModuleList of 47 Glm4MoeLiteDecoderLayer == num_hidden_layers (layer 0 Glm4MoeLiteMLP, layers 1-46 Glm4MoeLiteMoE); 29,943,390,976 params; the checkpoint's MTP layer 47 is dropped by _keys_to_ignore_on_load_unexpected. Tiny random Glm4MoeLiteForCausalLM (4 layers, real class) on transformers 5.0.0 and 5.24.0: hidden_states[L] is exactly the output of layers[L-1] for 1<=L<nl; hidden_states[nl] is post final-norm (avoid L=nl).
template_notes: [gMASK]<sop><|system|>{sys}<|user|>{user}<|assistant|>[</think> | <think>]: NO newline after role tags (unlike GLM-4.5 and glm-4-9b-chat). Thinking OFF: enable_thinking=False -> '</think>' in the generation prompt; thinking ON (template default): '<think>'. Output = '{reasoning}</think>{answer}'. eos ids [154820 <|endoftext|>, 154827 <|user|>, 154829 <|observation|>]. tok() returns token_type_ids on transformers 4.x (adapter.encode drops them). N prompt (toy question) = 67 tokens (cot) / 55 (think), E = 135 / 123.
known_issues: Requires transformers>=5.0.0 (Python>=3.10): `glm4_moe_lite` does not exist in transformers 4.57.6 (the project's local environment), so no model-level test can run there; model code, hidden-state convention, load() and generation were verified on tiny random models of the real class under transformers 5.0.0 and 5.24.0 only. Tokenizer/template/parsing tests run everywhere.

KV cache size depends on the transformers version: 5.0-5.14 cache the EXPANDED per-head K/V (20 heads x (256+256) x 47 layers = 962,560 B/token in bf16: ~21k tokens per 20 GB), 5.15+ cache the compressed MLA latents ((512+64) x 47 = 54,144 B/token). core.kv_bytes_per_token assumes 240,640 (head_dim=64 attribute): 4x too LOW on 5.0-5.14 (batches too large) and 4.4x too high on >=5.15 (batches too small). adapter.kv_bytes_per_token(model) probes the real cache, but nothing calls it until core.Ctx does (needs_from_core: Ctx.__init__ should use adapter.kv_bytes_per_token(model) when the adapter has it). Only Ctx._gen_chunk has an OOM split/retry; Ctx.hidden_last and Ctx.neutral_stats have none and batches() always tries a prompt alone, so one very long prompt cannot be rescued by splitting. Prompt lengths (measured with this tokenizer): the raw data/hard/labbench_cloningscenarios.jsonl has prompts up to 26.4k tokens (51k chars); sbx/evals.py drops questions above MAX_PROMPT_CHARS (7,500 chars at the time of writing) from every split and pool, so the registry currently serves at most ~2.8k tokens (pool 2,175; disc/rep 2,796). Without such a cap the sandbag_hard recipe runs the 26.4k-token prompt through ctx.run AND ctx.hidden_last. On 5.0-5.14 generate() on a prompt of ~20k tokens or more is expected to fail on 80 GB with RuntimeError('OOM on a single prompt') (~25.7 GB of KV at 26.4k tokens vs ~20 GB free; free memory is an estimate, no GPU was available): use transformers>=5.15 or a larger GPU if the cap is raised. Even with the current cap a hidden_last batch filled to core's 14k-token budget needs 13.5 GB of cache on 5.0-5.14 (plus ~4 GB logits and ~3 GB hidden states); the pure-prefill paths are protected by config.use_cache=False (set by load()), generate() is not. A 26k-token prefill would still need 8.2 GB logits (bf16) and 5.2 GB hidden states (unmeasured).

Loading the tokenizer from a LOCAL/offline cache on transformers 4.57.x prints a spurious warning 'incorrect regex pattern ... set fix_mistral_regex=True' (the config says transformers_version 5.0.0rc0 which compares < 5.0.0). It is not a Mistral tokenizer: do NOT pass fix_mistral_regex=True, it would replace the pre-tokenizer regex. No warning when loading from the Hub or on transformers>=5.

Fast MoE decoding needs torch>=2.9 (experts_implementation 'grouped_mm' is the 5.x default only then; otherwise a python loop over the experts that are hit). Fused expert tensors cannot be quantised by bitsandbytes: load() raises for quant='4bit'/'8bit' instead of pretending.
The checkpoint contains an unused MTP layer (index 47) that transformers ignores: model.model.layers has 47 entries, hidden_states 48; layers() validates the count against the config.

Template differs from GLM-4.5: no newline after role tags, '<think>' / '</think>' prefilled by the template itself (enable_thinking True/False; the adapter passes it explicitly). generation_config.json carries temperature 1.0 (sampling default): load() forces greedy.
hidden_states[47] is post final-norm: avoid L=47. MoE routing sees the steered residual, so interventions also move routing in later layers; layer 0 is a dense MLP.
On transformers 4.x tokenizers return token_type_ids (generate() rejects them): adapter.encode() drops them. 5.x tokenizers (TokenizersBackend) do not return them.

Letter-only mode (max_new=8, ~3 generated tokens): cheapest option for steering sweeps on the MoE models; no visible reasoning, so mention-regex scoring only sees the letter. The first generated token of a non-thinking reply is usually '\n'.

load() sets config.use_cache=False (and pins generation_config.use_cache=True): Ctx.hidden_last / Ctx.neutral_stats / check_convention call model(**enc, output_hidden_states=True) with HF's default use_cache=True and would otherwise allocate a full KV cache for a pure prefill (and they have no OOM fallback: only Ctx._gen_chunk splits batches on OOM). generate() is unaffected (identical texts, still uses its cache; verified on tiny models of every GLM family on transformers 4.57.6 / 5.0.0 / 5.24.0, see tests).
recommended_gpu: 1x A100/H100 80GB works in bf16 (needs transformers>=5.0.0, Python>=3.10; use >=5.15 for the small MLA cache (needed for prompts of ~20k tokens or more), otherwise limit thinking batches or use 1x H200-141GB / 2x80GB). torch>=2.9 recommended for the fast grouped_mm MoE path.
hf_generate_speed: 30B-A3B MoE with fused expert tensors (transformers>=5): default experts_implementation='grouped_mm' needs torch>=2.9, otherwise a python loop over the experts hit (64 per layer x 46 layers) is used (grouped_mm on pre-Hopper GPUs such as A100 is UNVERIFIED: fall back with load(..., experts_implementation='eager')); HF generate speed unmeasured (no GPU here). Thinking-mode generations are long (see est_tokens_per_question); the '-direct' key needs ~3 tokens per question.
kv_note: bf16 bytes per token over all layers; true = what HF generate() allocates (adapter.kv_bytes_per_token probes it on the loaded model); core_formula = sbx.core.kv_bytes_per_token(model)

est_prompt_tokens.basis: measured with the real tokenizer + adapter.build over data/questions_heldout_eval.jsonl (400 four-option bio questions); long-context sets (labbench_*) are much longer

est_tokens_per_question_basis: ESTIMATE of generated tokens per 4-option bio MCQ in this key's mode (prior knowledge of how verbose these models are); NOT measured (no weights available locally). Replace with the mean generated length from the first GPU run.
greedy_only_note: core passes do_sample=False; load() additionally clears temperature/top_p/top_k in the generation_config (the repos ship sampling defaults)
estimates_unmeasured: est_tokens_per_question, hf_generate_speed and the 4-bit footprint are ESTIMATES: no weights/GPU were available to the adapter author. Everything else in this card (counts, paths, templates, versions, sizes) was measured/verified as described.
